kapak.alt: High-frequency loss erases place of articulation

youtube.baslik: Which speech cue is lost first in high-frequency hearing loss? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In Miller and Nicely's 1955 study, voicing and nasality cues were largely preserved in noise and when high frequencies were filtered out. Place of articulation was the cue most easily lost, so sounds that differ only in place, like s and sh, can be confused with high-frequency hearing loss.

instagram.kanca: Which speech cue is lost first in high-frequency hearing loss?
bilgiler: With high-frequency loss, voicing and nasality cues are largely preserved.
The cue lost most easily is place of articulation.
S and sh differ only in place, which is carried at high frequencies.

cumleler: Which speech cue is lost first in high-frequency hearing loss?
Consonants are defined by place, manner and voicing.
With high-frequency loss, voicing and nasality cues are largely preserved.
Place of articulation, where the sound is made, is lost most easily.

cumleler.yazi: The sounds s and sh differ only in place of articulation.
cumleler.ses: The sounds ess and shh differ only in place of articulation.

cumleler.yazi: B and p, which differ only in voicing, hold up better.
cumleler.ses: Bee and pee, which differ only in voicing, hold up better.
